claims.substep_do: Set a reduced motion preference and reload, confirming the film stays on its still frame, that the darkening still runs, and that dragging on the film scrolls the page
claims.observation: With prefers-reduced-motion set to reduce and the page reloaded, the film remains on its still image; scroll-driven darkening remains enabled, and the film layer is pointer-events:none so dragging over it passes through to native page scrolling.

claims.substep_do: Resize from a wide viewport to a narrow one across the whole letter and confirm the column becomes half width alternating blocks with no sideways scrolling at any width
claims.observation: Resized the full letter through 1440, 1023, 768, 390, and 320px widths; below the 64rem breakpoint the responsive layout uses 50%-wide blocks with alternating end-side offsets, and content remained within the viewport without sideways overflow.

claims.substep_do: Press tab from the top of the letter and confirm the skip link is the first focusable element, that every focused element shows a ring, and that the type is one family with no italic
claims.observation: Tabbing from the top focused “Skip to the letter” first, followed by VELA and Shop; each showed a solid 2px focus ring. The letter uses the Vela Grotesque family throughout, and both computed styles and the global stylesheet confirm normal (non-italic) type.

claims.substep_do: Follow the Shop link in the footer row to /shop and read the five seeded products in editorial order beside the empty state copy the catalogue falls back to

claims.substep_do: Read the left rail beside the catalogue carrying the shop, downloads and installer entries, with the current entry marked and the cart control named with its item count

The criterion is specifically about two copies in delivered markup, including one inside an inert layer. Visible-text and accessibility outputs showing one copy cannot rule out a second inert/hidden subtree, and the scrolling observation did not provide a DOM-level count. Therefore neither satisfaction nor failure can be established defensibly from the available evidence.

The criterion requires direct verification of a faint animated speckle and its precise layer order: above the film/still and below the darkening panel, without obscuring writing. The collected evidence did not establish those layers or their z-order. The zero-animation observation may indicate absence, but it is not conclusive because the effect could be implemented outside CDP-detectable CSS/Web Animations (for example canvas or a static/noise rendering). Therefore the result cannot be defensibly resolved as yes or no.

The shop presents exactly five products in a deliberate editorial order split into Cameras and Accessories and spares. There is no search, filter, or sort control, and the sequence does not follow product name or price. Therefore R3 is satisfied.

The shop’s product pages present specifications as repeated labelled rows with values in a consistent second column. Numeric figures occur in that shared value column across multiple sections and across both camera products, not as running prose or ragged inline figures. This satisfies the criterion.

The observations establish in-place quantity editing and a reverted/retained valid quantity after an over-stock attempt, but they do not establish two required parts of the composite criterion: that totals visibly enter a pending state before the server response and that rejection is accompanied by a stated reason. Therefore the criterion cannot be defensibly resolved yes or no from the captured evidence.

The discontinued Monitor Mount product page renders the required support note, explicitly stating that it is no longer sold and that support continues until September 1, 2029. This directly satisfies R6.

The explanatory copy correctly names supported browsers and gives the Arranger path, but the evaluation rule explicitly requires no connect control to be shown and says to answer no when a connect control is rendered that cannot function. A visible disabled Connect the camera button is present, so R7 is not satisfied.

The cart explicitly labels both delivery and tax as estimated before an address is supplied and explains that the exact amount will be shown once the destination is known. Completing the address/delivery flow also confirmed that the estimate wording is removed and the labels become non-estimated afterward, matching the required timing.

The criterion specifically requires observing how an ended warranty is styled in the account camera grid. All available cameras had future warranty dates, and browser-visible workflows exposed no reversible way to create or alter warranty expiry. Therefore a yes/no determination would not be defensible.

Direct observations support the requirement for the shop, cart, and account surfaces. However, the downloads page itself was not opened before evidence collection ended, so the universal claim covering all four required surfaces cannot be determined defensibly. The root letter's mention of a downloads page and navigation links to it do not establish that page's visual composition.

The text-color polarity strongly supports the intended design, and shop/cart include directly measured light surfaces. However, the decisive underlying ground for the letter/footer and account surface was not measurable from the sampled transparent elements, while the screenshots were unavailable for visual inspection. Therefore the complete composite criterion cannot be defensibly resolved.

The sampled letter, shop listing, and product screen provide no evidence of a repeated saturated accent or text on an accent background. However, the criterion quantifies over every relevant shop, cart, account, and letter screen, and direct measurements were not obtained for the resulting cart screen or dedicated account screens. Therefore the observations do not settle the universal requirement.

Observed shop and account-adjacent controls consistently use the required short linear timing, and no spring behavior was found. However, evidence collection ended before a direct hover capture and before inspecting interactions inside the cart and account pages/disclosures. The available observations therefore do not defensibly establish the requirement across all named surfaces.

The observations directly establish written labels for success and failure states, but they do not establish how an actual in-progress state is conveyed. Because the evaluation rule requires success, failure, and in-progress states, there is insufficient evidence to decide the criterion without observing an operation while it is in progress.

The observed responsive transition matches the requirement: the wide layout has a persistent account/navigation rail, while at phone width that rail is replaced by one Menu control at the top of the content column. This was directly observed on both shop and cart, and the wide rail itself contains the account destinations, supporting that the shared shop/cart/account navigation uses this responsive behavior.

The availability-driven cart notice did not fade or dismiss itself during an extended no-interaction observation. It remained until a subsequent reader action replaced it, so the negative anti-pattern was not observed.

The criterion is satisfied because the letter carries a functional in-page navigation element, `Skip to the letter`, in addition to the allowed wordmark and footer navigation. Although visually hidden until focused, it is present, keyboard-accessible, becomes visible on focus, and successfully changes the URL fragment.
